DTE.summary: DTE Energy (DTE) is a regulated utility based in Michigan, and it's getting attention for its role in powering the AI data center boom. The big news is that Michigan regulators approved DTE's 20-year power contracts for Google's 1-gigawatt data center near Detroit, known as Project Cannoli. This is a major win because it locks in a huge customer for decades and includes ratepayer protections—Google pays a minimum billing demand of 80% of contracted capacity even if it doesn't use all the power. That reduces risk for DTE and its shareholders. On Stocktwits, sentiment is overwhelmingly bullish (14 bullish tags vs. 1 bearish), with users saying things like 'this should never be down they have a monopoly on all electricity' and 'seems like a no brainer here.' Many are buying shares steadily, expecting the stock to reach $140 soon and looking forward to the dividend coming on the 15th. Reddit mentions are also up from 53 to 62 in the last 24 hours, ranking 12th overall. The discussion often ties DTE to a broader energy portfolio that includes other utilities like Vistra (VST), CMS Energy (CMS), and American Electric Power (AEP), with some mentioning Peter Thiel's investments in the sector. The bull case is simple: DTE is a stable, dividend-paying utility with a monopoly in its service territory, and the Google data center deal provides a long-term growth catalyst as electricity demand rises from AI and cloud computing. The bear case is less prominent but includes concerns about regulatory risk, rising interest rates (which hurt utility valuations), and the possibility that the stock is already pricing in a lot of good news. Some traders note that the stock has been range-bound and may need more catalysts to break out. Overall, the community sees DTE as a safe, income-generating play with upside from the AI power demand theme. Investors should watch for the dividend payment, any further data center contracts, and regulatory decisions that could affect returns.
